'Paṇḍitānaṃ' (from Khuddaka Nikāya 319) refers to those who are wise (paṇḍita) - those who proceed with wisdom (ñāṇagatiyā) in matters both visible here and now (sandiṭṭhika) and pertaining to the future (samparāyika).
The term paṇḍita is derived in several ways:
1. From paṇḍa + ita: One who has progressed through the wisdom of the highest path (aggamaggapaññā)
2. From paṇḍā + ita: One who is wise through four causes
3. One who knows phenomena (sabhāvadhamma) according to their true nature
A paṇḍita is:
- One who knows through wisdom (paññā)
- One who proceeds through knowledge (ñāṇagatiyā)
- One who has developed wisdom naturally
- One who understands both worldly and spiritual matters
- One who possesses discriminative understanding
